framework: China - Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services (Order No. 15, in force 15 Aug 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Violations handled under Cybersecurity, Data Security, PIPL and S&T Progress laws; otherwise warnings, public criticism, correction orders, and possible service suspension.
what_is_tested: Enforcement

framework: China - Interim Measures for Anthropomorphic AI Interactive Services (Order No. 21; promulgated 10 Apr 2026; in force 15 Jul 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must complete algorithm filing under algorithm rules; national authority promotes an AI sandbox security service platform that providers are encouraged to join for security testing.
what_is_tested: Algorithm filing; voluntary sandbox testing

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Systems must achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity consistently throughout their lifecycle, and accuracy levels and metrics must be declared in the instructions for use.
what_is_tested: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity performance

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Sandboxes give a controlled environment for development, training, testing and validation under an agreed sandbox plan; authorities give guidance and supervision to identify risks, and on request supply written proof and an exit report which market surveillance authorities and notified bodies must take positively into account.
what_is_tested: Pre-market testing and validation under regulator supervision

framework: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1755 (arrangements under Reg. (EU) 2024/1689 Arts 92(6), 101(6))
requirement_paraphrase: Independent experts evaluating GPAI models for the Commission must be independent of providers (shared ownership, governance, staff or resources and contracts with the provider over at least the prior 12 months are considered), declare interests, and keep confidentiality and information-security protocols; providers may submit reasoned observations on appointed experts; experts are selected by call for expressions of interest (standing list possible), directly from the scientific panel, or under the Financial Regulation.
what_is_tested: Independence and selection of external evaluators of GPAI models

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: To support post-market monitoring, signatories give an adequate number of independent external evaluators free access to the most capable model version on the market, its chains-of-thought if available, and the least-mitigated corresponding version (unless the model is similarly safe or safer), publish selection criteria, do not train on evaluators' test inputs/outputs without permission, and take no legal or technical retaliation against evaluators who test and publish findings within stated limits.
what_is_tested: Third-party post-market evaluation access and safe harbour

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Technical report on properties, risks, methods and processes for AI in safety functions, non-AI safety functions protecting AI-controlled equipment, and AI used to develop safety functions; published Jan 2024, 73 pages.
what_is_tested: Functional safety aspects of AI

framework: Japan AISI - Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety v1.10 (28 Mar 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Defines ten evaluation perspectives: toxic output control; misinformation and manipulation; fairness and inclusion; high-risk/unintended use; privacy; security; explainability; robustness; data quality; verifiability.
what_is_tested: Ten safety perspectives for LLM systems
who_tests: Development and provision managers; experts inside or outside the organisation; third-party evaluation can complement (Sec. 4.1)

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems posing high risk to basic rights must undergo pre- and post-conformity assessments in addition to ethics adherence and statutory requirements; unacceptable-risk systems are not allowed.
what_is_tested: Conformity with ethics and statutory requirements (before and after deployment)

framework: NCA 'Draft of AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' (AICG-1:2026), draft for public consultation (closed 5 Aug 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Continuously assess the cybersecurity capabilities and resilience of AI agents throughout the development lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Cybersecurity capabilities and resilience of AI agents

framework: Singapore Project Moonshot (AI Verify Foundation)
requirement_paraphrase: Open-source toolkit that assesses safety and reliability of LLMs/apps through benchmark testing and red teaming; described as implementing the benchmarks recommended in IMDA's Starter Kit.
what_is_tested: LLM benchmarks and red teaming
who_tests: Developers and deployers using the toolkit

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Entities must run internal audits and assessments to verify compliance and report compliance status to DoH; DoH will conduct periodic audits and technical assessments of regulated entities.
what_is_tested: Compliance with the Standard

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations Reg 10 / Commissioner materials Accreditation and Certification Framework
clause_or_page: D p.5 'Why is the Framework necessary?'; p.4
requirement_paraphrase: Framework says the Regulations bar commercial use of Systems for High Risk Processing unless audit and certification requirements are met; applicant defined as 'Certification Applicant'.
what_is_tested: Compliance of High Risk Processing Systems with certification requirements

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Guidelines (Smart Dubai v1.11, English)
requirement_paraphrase: Developers and operators should undertake reasonable data exploration and/or testing to identify potentially prejudicial decision making tendencies arising from data bias.
what_is_tested: Training/input data for bias; resulting decision tendencies
who_tests: AI developer organisations and AI operator organisations (self)

framework: Information Security Regulation v2.0 (DESC)
requirement_paraphrase: Organisations implement a security sign off process to confirm proper implementation of security controls.
what_is_tested: Implementation of security controls before deployment

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Operators should assure end users of reliability through documentation, including operationalising processes for testing and verification of desired outcomes.
what_is_tested: System reliability and desired outcomes

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: Understand how to monitor and mitigate drift, bias and (for generative AI) hallucinations and have a robust testing and monitoring process to catch them.
what_is_tested: Drift, bias, hallucination monitoring

framework: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
clause_or_page: Research Agenda: Introduction > 'Our Approach to Research and Impact'; Risks Research > 'Generalised effective measurement risk research' (Science of Evaluations)
requirement_paraphrase: AISI aims to distil findings into best practices, standards and protocols, and researches the 'science of evaluations' so that measurements of frontier capability are accurate, robust and decision-useful.
what_is_tested: Evaluation science and best-practice development

framework: US NIST AI RMF Playbook (AIRC; companion to AI RMF 1.0)
requirement_paraphrase: Playbook suggestions are voluntary; it is neither a checklist nor a set of steps to follow in full; organisations may borrow as many or as few as fit.
what_is_tested: n/a (status of Playbook)

framework: US NIST CAISSI program page (nist.gov/caisi; titled 'Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI)' as retrieved 2026-10-16; formerly CAISI)
requirement_paraphrase: The centre states it will develop guidelines and best practices and help industry develop voluntary standards, establish voluntary agreements with private sector SI developers and evaluators, and lead unclassified evaluations of SI capabilities that may pose national security risks, focusing on demonstrable risks such as cybersecurity, biosecurity and chemical weapons.
what_is_tested: National-security-relevant capabilities of frontier systems (cyber, bio, chemical)
